facts: Preeti Gupta and another filed an appeal against the impugned judgment of the High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi, Jharkhand dated 27.4.2009 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Petition Nos.304 of 2009.

The complainant Manisha was married to Kamal Poddar at Kanpur on 10.12.2006 and immediately after the marriage, she left for Mumbai along with her husband who was working with Tata Consultancy Services (for short "TCS") and was permanently residing at Mumbai.
Respondent no.2 visited Ranchi to participate in 'Gangaur' festival on 16.3.2007 and returned to Mumbai on 24.03.2007.

The complainant filed a complaint on 08.07.2007 before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi under sections 498-A, 406, 341, 323 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code read with ss.3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act against all immediate relations of her husband.
The appellants are aggrieved by the said summoning order.
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in not exercising its inherent powers u/s.482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the facts and circumstances of this case?
petitioner_arguments: There were no specific allegations against both the appellants in the complaint.

Appellant no.1 had been permanently residing with her husband at Navasari, Surat (Gujarat) for the last more than seven years and had never visited Mumbai during the year 2007 and never stayed with respondent no.2 or her husband.
Appellant no.2 was permanent resident of Goregaon, Maharashtra and had also been permanently residing there for a number of years.
The appellants had never interfered with the internal affairs of the complainant and her husband.
They had been falsely implicated in this case.
respondent_arguments: The acts relating to demand or subjecting to cruelty, as per the complaint petition, have been committed at the place where the complainant was living with her husband.

The complainant in her statement made under solemn affirmation has stated that when she came to Ranchi on the occasion of Holi, all the accused persons came and passed sarcastic remarks which in absence of actual wordings, according to the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner could never be presumed to be an act constituting offence under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
court_reasoning: The High Court has inherent power to act ex debito justitiae to do real and substantial justice, for the administration of which alone it exists, or to prevent abuse of the process of the court.
Inherent power u/s.482 Cr.P.C. can be exercised: (i) to give effect to an order under the Code; (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of court, and (iii) to otherwise secure the ends of justice.
The courts have consistently taken the view that they must use this extraordinary power to prevent injustice and secure the ends of justice.
holding: Leave granted. The appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment of the High Court is set aside.
